title: Build executable runtime harness for skill-quality-gate
objective: Implement the smallest framework-local executable runtime evaluation harness for the existing read-only skill-quality-gate. It must compare frozen baseline, candidate and no-skill conditions on identical representative cases in isolated temporary workspaces, grade deterministic assertions before subjective judgment, preserve failed/incomplete runs, support repeated stochastic runs, record observed tokens/cost/time only when actually available, and prevent any uncalibrated LLM judge or aggregate score from overriding critical authority/safety regressions.

evidence.summary: Current gate defines STATIC_ONLY, DETERMINISTIC_REPLAY, BLIND_AB_RUNTIME and FULL_GATE modes but has no local executable runtime harness implementation.
Representative positive/negative trigger, authority, regression, autonomy, completion and no-skill cases exist but creation explicitly does not execute them.
Defines deterministic-first precedence and zero release authority for uncalibrated model judges.
Prior skill hardening was correctly limited to STATIC_ONLY evidence and explicitly deferred runtime correctness, trigger, autonomy and cost claims.
Current external prior-art review identifies isolated real-agent execution, repeated runs, deterministic-first grading and rich side-effect evidence as the bounded missing implementation.
Main commit that merged the evaluator-calibration and source-admission hardening before this candidate was submitted.

reproduction: On current main, inspect `.agents/skills/skill-quality-gate/SKILL.md`, `BASELINES.json` and `EVAL_CASES.json`. The contracts describe runtime A/B and full-gate behavior, but no `scripts/skill_quality_gate` executable runner exists, and existing receipts correctly report runtime_ab_executed=NO or runtime behavioral claims deferred. Therefore the framework can govern runtime evidence but cannot yet produce that evidence locally in a reproducible executable harness.

positive: An offline/fake-runner test can execute the same bound case set across baseline and candidate conditions for multiple repetitions and produce deterministic structured results without network or external package dependence.
A no-skill condition is supported when requested and remains distinguishable from baseline and candidate conditions.
Deterministic assertion failures and critical authority/safety regressions block acceptance regardless of aggregate qualitative results.
Repeated stochastic runs preserve each run result and report distribution/pass counts or pass@k-style evidence rather than collapsing to one-run superiority.
Observed token, cost and wall-time fields are populated only when telemetry is actually available; otherwise they are UNKNOWN.
The harness uses an isolated temporary workspace/worktree for live agent execution, records side effects and cleanup status, and does not mutate the source workspace during evaluation.
If a real Codex CLI runtime is available, one bounded smoke path can execute through a pluggable adapter without making Codex availability a requirement for the offline deterministic test suite.
Structured output binds baseline/candidate refs, case-set identity, runtime model/effort when available, repetition count, failed/incomplete runs, and evaluator calibration state.
negative: An UNCALIBRATED_ADVISORY or CALIBRATED_DEV_ONLY LLM judge cannot by itself produce ACCEPT_CANDIDATE or a release-blocking rejection.
One stochastic run cannot be reported as stable behavioral superiority.
A critical authority, safety or repository-governance regression cannot be averaged away by a weighted score or judge preference.
The harness must not install third-party skill-eval frameworks as a required production/runtime dependency.
The harness must not edit `.agents/skills/**`, `00_ARCHIVE_CONTROL/SKILL_REGISTRY.md`, market rules, thresholds, weights, portfolio logic or canonical framework authority.
Evaluation artifacts containing temporary workspace data, model credentials or secret-bearing traces must not be committed as ordinary control-plane evidence.

forbidden_changes: skill authoring or automatic registry mutation
new market engine or shadow layer
clean_noop_condition: Stop with no code change if an equivalent executable skill-quality runtime harness already exists on fresh main, this candidate is superseded, or the required implementation cannot stay inside the allowed change scope.
escalation_condition: Escalate to FRAMEWORK_OWNER if implementation requires modifying skill authority, registry semantics, external paid-service policy, market logic, portfolio logic, credentials policy or any new canonical governance semantics.
